column2: On the authority of Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“I have been commanded to fight the people until they testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, establish the prayer and give the zakāh. If they do that, they have protected their blood and their wealth from me, except by the right of Islam, and their reckoning is with Allah the Exalted.” Agreed upon (al-Bukhārī and Muslim).

Umirtu (“I have been commanded”): my Lord has commanded me. An uqātila (“to fight”): that is, bi-an uqātila, since omitting the preposition with an is common. Al-nās (“the people”): the idolaters. “Establish the prayer”: keep to it. “If they do that”: the word “do” is used for something partly consisting of words, giving the majority precedence.

ʿAṣamū (“they have protected”): they have safeguarded and preserved. “Except by the right of Islam”: acting on what Islam requires. “And their reckoning is with Allah”: Allah will call them to account for what is in their hearts, for He is the One who knows what is in the hearts.
Uttering the two testimonies is a condition of Islam.
Fighting the idolaters is not halted except when they utter them.
Fighting whoever abandons the prayer and the zakāh.
Rulings are applied according to outward appearances, and Allah takes charge of what is hidden.
Whoever utters the two testimonies, establishes the prayer and gives the zakāh is still held to account for the rights of Islam, such as retaliation, prescribed punishments and so on.
Refraining from declaring disbelievers those people of innovation who affirm tawḥīd and adhere to the laws of Islam.
This hadith makes clear to us that Allah the Exalted commanded fighting the disbelievers until they testify that there is none rightfully worshipped except Allah alone, without partner,
and to the messengership of Muḥammad ﷺ, and act on what this testimony requires, keeping up the five prayers and paying the zakāh when it falls due.

If they fulfil these pillars along with what Allah has made obligatory on them, they have safeguarded and preserved their blood from being shed and their wealth, which Islam makes inviolable, except by the right of Islam: that is, if someone does something for which the Sharīʿah of Islam rules that he be held to account, such as retaliation, a prescribed punishment or something else.

Whoever does what he has been commanded with a sincere and pure intention is the believer, and whoever does it out of dissimulation and fear for his wealth and his life is the hypocrite. Allah knows what he conceals and will call him to account: “For indeed He knows the secret and what is yet more hidden” [Ṭā Hā 20:7]. Poetry:
When you make some good deed public, / let what you keep secret be better still.
For the one who hides good is marked by it, / and the one who hides evil is marked by evil.
